subject: Cannot graph Quadratic Models or include them in AIC

messages.author: 67eefb0e32c64fae
messages.subject: Cannot graph Quadratic Models or include them in AIC
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to model Dayscore as a quadratic predictor of detection probability. However, when I use the predict function, there is a big block of NA values produced for my SE and CIs. This means I cannot use it in my AIC analysis, and my graphs look very funky! Has anyone encountered this issue? Is there a solution? I have a deadline coming up and will just abandon quadratics if not... :(

Code:

#Dynamic Model (DP is a quadratic function of Dayscore (May 15th))
  fm5 <- colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, epsilonformula = ~1, pformula = ~obs.dayscore + I(obs.dayscore^2), data = FosnUMF, se = TRUE)
  newdata.5 <- data.frame(obs.dayscore = seq(8, 122, by = 1))
  fm5.ds <- predict(fm5, newdata=newdata.5, type="det", appendData=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Cannot graph Quadratic Models or include them in AIC
parts:
After a lot of outside consultation, looks like it was the "I" function causing issues. Not only was it causing the NaNs to pop up, but it was inflating my detection estimates in predict as well.

New code below (basically just with "I" removed):

fm5 <- colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, epsilonformula = ~1, pformula = ~(obs.dayscore + (obs.dayscore^2)), data = FosnUMF, se = TRUE)
  range(obs.dayscore,na.rm=TRUE)

newdata.5 <- data.frame(obs.dayscore = seq(8, 122, by = 1))
  fm5.ds <- predict(fm5, newdata=newdata.5, type="det", appendData=TRUE)
  fm5.ds
